name: Altstadt
tagline: The medieval centre, with the inhabited bridge running through it
description: One of the largest intact medieval centres in Germany, built around the cathedral hill, the Fischmarkt and the Kramerbrucke, a bridge lined with houses along its whole length. It survived the war, so the timber framing is original. Restaurants, the market and the tram lines all sit inside it.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to live inside the medieval town rather than visit it
pros: The Kramerbrucke, cathedral and market all within ten minutes
Trams from the centre in every direction
The best restaurant and cafe density in the city
cons: Visitor traffic around the bridge and cathedral
Old buildings with variable insulation and no parking

name: Andreasviertel
tagline: Timber-framed lanes north of the cathedral, quiet and restored
description: The old craftsmen's quarter northwest of the cathedral, a grid of narrow lanes with restored timber-framed houses, small bars and a strong neighbourhood identity. It is inside the historic centre but off the visitor routes, which makes it noticeably calmer than the streets around the Kramerbrucke.
bestFor: Stays that want the old town without the day-visitor traffic
pros: Restored timber-framed streets with real character
Five minutes from the cathedral, well off the tourist route
Small bars and a genuine local scene

name: Kraempfervorstadt and Johannesvorstadt
tagline: Wilhelminian blocks east of the centre, the best everyday value
description: The nineteenth century residential districts east of the old town, built as apartment blocks with high ceilings and street trees, now largely renovated. Local shops, bars and the trams into the centre are all here, and rents sit clearly below the Altstadt for a better standard of flat.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a proper flat at a rent that makes sense
pros: High-ceilinged period apartments at moderate rents
Ten minutes by tram or on foot to the centre
Local bars, bakeries and everyday shopping
cons: Renovation quality varies block to block
Some traffic on the main radial roads
Less atmospheric than the old town

name: Steigerwald and Hochheim
tagline: The forest edge on the southern slope
description: The southern districts where the city runs up against the Steigerwald, a large forest with marked paths that begins at the last row of houses. Housing is a mix of villas and post-war blocks, quieter and greener than anything central, with the trams reaching the lower end of it.
bestFor: Stays where a forest run before work matters more than a bar downstairs
pros: Forest trails directly from the doorstep
Genuinely quiet and noticeably fresher air
Fifteen minutes by tram to the centre
cons: Uphill in both directions on foot

name: Rieth and the Northern Estates
tagline: Panel estates north of the centre, the cheapest rents
description: The socialist-era housing estates built north of the city, with their own shops, schools and clinics, a lake and park in the middle and frequent trams into town. The architecture is uniform and the rents are the lowest in Erfurt by a clear margin, which for a long stay is the point.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: The lowest rents in the city
Full everyday shopping and a park with a lake
Direct tram into the centre in fifteen minutes
cons: Nothing to walk to in the evening
Feels a long way from the medieval city
